notes: DIVOC (Digital Infrastructure for Vaccination & Open Credentialing) is a self-hosted digital public good for issuing verifiable vaccination certificates; each deployment runs its own host, so the adaptor takes baseUrl from the credential and servers[0] is the vendor's own reference host from the spec's host/basePath. openapi.json is the lossless 3.0.3 conversion of the vendor's Swagger 2.0 interfaces/vaccination-api.yaml — 23 operations and 11 definitions upstream, 23 operations and 11 schemas derived, nothing dropped — replacing a hand-authored single-endpoint subset. The vendor's repository (egovernments/DIVOC) was archived and no longer serves raw files, so the upstream bytes came from the Internet Archive's snapshot of the vendor's own raw URL (india branch, captured 2022-05-20) and are committed verbatim; the spec's own version is 1.0.0 and a later DIVOC release could differ, which is why the specUrl recorded is the archived one that still resolves. The vaccination API is the surface the adaptor talks to; DIVOC's separate admin/registry portal interfaces are outside this spec's (and the vendor file's) scope and are not archived anywhere we could find. Three $refs in the vendor file point at sibling files the vendor never shipped in interfaces/ (../registry/Vaccinator.json, ../registry/RecipientSideEffects.json); they are grounded in openapi.json to an empty schema carrying a 'Type not documented' description, which is the same convention the Swagger converter applies to a dangling #/definitions ref, and a self-reference (./vaccination-api.yaml#/definitions/Error) is resolved to the Error schema in the same document. The committed upstream.yaml is untouched. Cross-reference: the adaptor's only network call, certifyVaccination -> POST /v1/certify, is present; note that the vendor spec types that request body as an ARRAY of CertificationRequest while the adaptor passes whatever the job supplies (its JSDoc example passes a single object), and the mock sandbox accepts both. Two mock endpoints have no counterpart here and are recorded as findings for the mocker rather than additions to a converted spec: GET /v1/certificate/{certificateId} (the vendor spec has GET /v1/certificates for the caller's own certificate, PUT /v1/certificate and DELETE /v1/certificates/{preEnrollmentCode}) and the Keycloak token endpoint POST /auth/realms/divoc/protocol/openid-connect/token, which belongs to the bundled Keycloak rather than to the DIVOC API.
